answer: Every fresh alias dilutes the cluster's average standing, so the larger the flock the weaker each individual vote becomes — coordination requires many low-weight votes that cancel each other out. The key insight is that coordination itself leaks: the more unified a farm is, the more easily its shared style or timing betrays it. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation. Consider a sonnet as the anchor of the cost.
